title: The Kiln Room
subtitle: A fire that started twice
briefing: A fire destroys the glazing shed at a ceramics works. The insurance claim is substantial and the business was three months from closure. The fire investigator's report finds two separate points of origin, which rules out an accident. Four people held keys to the site.
solution: Marguerite Halden set the fire herself to recover the value of a business she could not sell. She used the kiln's own timer to create a delayed second point of origin, giving herself a clean alibi at a restaurant eleven miles away. The night watchman's late arrival and the electrician's unfinished rewiring were both genuine and both irrelevant.

suspects.name: Marguerite Halden
suspects.motive: The business was three months from closure and heavily insured.

statements.question: Where were you that night?
statements.text: At the Fern and Anchor from nine until eleven. Eleven miles away.

statements.question: Who holds a site key?
statements.text: Four of us. Myself, Joe, the electrician, and the kiln technician.

statements.question: Was the kiln in use?
statements.text: It was shut down for the weekend. It had been cold since Friday.

suspects.name: Joe Merrick
suspects.motive: Arrived forty minutes late and did not report it.

statements.question: Where were you that night?
statements.text: I was late. Forty minutes. I have never been late in nine years and I am sick about it.

statements.question: Who holds a site key?
statements.text: Four keys. Mine is on my belt and always has been.

statements.question: Was the kiln in use?
statements.text: Cold since Friday. I checked it on my Saturday round.

suspects.name: Sam Iqbal
suspects.motive: The rewiring was unfinished and left exposed connections.

statements.question: Where were you that night?
statements.text: At home from six. My last visit to site was Thursday.

statements.question: Who holds a site key?
statements.text: I hold one while the job runs. I hand it back at the end.

statements.question: Was the kiln in use?
statements.text: I do not touch the kiln circuits. That is a separate contract.

suspects.name: Ruth Okoye
suspects.motive: Programmed the kiln controller the week before.

statements.question: Where were you that night?
statements.text: At home. I finished the Friday service at four and left.

statements.question: Who holds a site key?
statements.text: Four. Mine has not left the works, I keep it in the plant room.

statements.question: Was the kiln in use?
statements.text: I left a schedule on the controller. It should not have fired without a manual start.

locations.name: Glazing Shed
locations.description: What is left of it. Two areas of deep charring, ten metres apart.

searchables.label: Examine the second point of origin

searchables.label: Inspect the new wiring
searchables.flavour: Unfinished, but isolated at the board.

locations.name: Kiln Room

searchables.label: Read the kiln controller

searchables.label: Read the service log

searchables.flavour: Forty minutes late, and honest about it.

searchables.flavour: Three months of runway, at best.

evidence.name: First point of origin
evidence.description: An accelerant pattern near the shed door, ignited first.

evidence.name: Delayed second origin
evidence.description: A second origin at the kiln wall that began roughly an hour later.

evidence.name: Unfinished wiring
evidence.description: The new wiring is incomplete but isolated at the distribution board.

evidence.name: Kiln controller record
evidence.description: A manual start was programmed for 12:15 AM.

evidence.name: Service log entry
evidence.description: An entry after the technician's Friday service, in a different hand.

evidence.name: Late sign-on
evidence.description: The watchman signed on forty minutes late and recorded it himself.

evidence.name: Barrier vehicle log
evidence.description: A vehicle entered at 11:20 PM and left at 11:34 PM.

evidence.name: Accounts position
evidence.description: The works had three months of runway remaining.

evidence.name: Increased cover
evidence.description: The insurance cover was increased seven weeks before the fire.

evidence.name: Restaurant bill
evidence.description: The bill was settled at 10:52 PM, not at eleven.

evidence.name: Restaurant staff account
evidence.description: Staff recall the table leaving noticeably early.

evidence.name: Vehicle identification
evidence.description: The barrier record identifies the owner's car.

timeline.text: A restaurant bill is settled eleven miles away.
The first fire is set near the shed door.
The night watchman signs on, forty minutes late.
The kiln controller executes a programmed start.

hints: Two points of origin means two decisions, not one accident.
One of them started an hour after the other. Ask what could do that on a timer.
Check the alibi's timestamp rather than the alibi's owner.
